items.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: To be in the same space that Mel Lewis, that young big band recorded, and to become a not close friend, but a friend of Max Gordan and meet all those people there

ctx.x: And that first record, where did it enable you to play that you had never played before?

I play the Village Vanguard, for example; that for me was like a dream come true, playing in front of the big picture of John Coltrane that they have there. To be in the same space that Mel Lewis, that young big band recorded, and to become a not close friend, but a friend of Max Gordan and meet all those people there, so I play the Village Vanguard, I play the Blue Note, and all over the place.
